examples: It's a nice house. She's a lawyer. (saying what something is / what somebody does)
I saw an old man with a dog. The dog was barking. (first mention, then the)
The moon goes round the Earth. (only one of something)
It's the best restaurant in town. (superlative)
I love flowers, but I hate the flowers in my garden. (general vs specific)
She's not at home today. I get back from work at five thirty. (home / work after at / from)
I never have breakfast. See you next week. (meals; next + week)
grammar.explanation: Use a or an with singular countable nouns: to say what something is or what somebody does (She's a lawyer), the first time you mention a thing or person (I saw an old man with a dog), in What...! exclamations (What an awful day!), and in expressions of frequency (three times a week). Use the when you talk about something you already mentioned (The dog was barking), when it is clear what you mean (The bell rang and my father opened the door), when there is only one of something (the moon), with places in a town (the cinema, the theatre), and with superlatives (the best restaurant). Use no article when you speak in general with plural and uncountable nouns (I love flowers; Love is more important than money), with home, work, school, church after at / to / from (She's not at home today), before meals, days and months (I never have breakfast), and before next / last + day, week, etc. (See you next week).
